body.statement: Every `Gate::admit` attempt either admits or routes exactly one refusal reason to its saturating counter: cooldown first, then rate, then capacity. Admission increments no refusal counter; refusing creates no new cooldown or rate slot. Before any category saturates, attempted count equals admissions plus the three refusal counts.

An opt-in forwarding deadline is checked before connection/backoff work and after handshake, immediately before preparing a send/retry. Expired FIFO entries are removed in pairs and increment `expired`, never a node-answer result. Each removal spends flush work budget. Source TTL entries still render retractions and require ACK; expired entries behind an unexpired FIFO head wait until they reach the front.

body.evidence_text: `oversized_audit_records_are_counted_and_marked_before_following_data_or_flush` (real asynchronous writer, chained file, metrics and CLI)
body.statement: Oversized records are known losses, not successful appends. Before following data or sync, `AUDIT_LOST` accounts for them even on a still-writable log.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 3, 2026-10-10): a one-slot peer flooded 262144 non-expiring claims into the shared MAX_KNOWN_CLAIMS memory; its envelope held, yet this node's own detection and a third node's claim were refused for good. Owner chose design A (ADR-0025).

body.statement: A peer's claims known here, enforced or waiting, never exceed its envelope's known-claims share, and peers' claims together leave the room kept for this node's own decisions: no volume from one peer makes this node refuse its own detections or another peer's claims.
Admission counts missing records, not all claims: a full global record table can update a suitable existing record. A still-held event requires no new claim/tombstone storage.

body.evidence_text: `a_detection_refused_at_capacity_leaves_no_event_and_no_strike` (mutations "remember the event first" and "count the strike first" each fail it).
body.statement: A detection checks its event id, adds or merges the claim, then records the event, under one table lock. A resend of an event acted on within EVENT_MEMORY is a duplicate. A refused detection (here: the known-claims cap) records no event and counts no strike: a resend after capacity frees is decided afresh, and the next block of that target gets the TTL of its first strike.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 2, 2026-10-10): 203.0.113.5 and ::ffff:203.0.113.5 were two keys of the cooldown set, so one host was admitted twice at one Instant under a 60 s cooldown, while the node reads both as one host. Fix: the source address is canonical from parsing on.

body.statement: Successful admissions of one source IP are separated by at least cooldown. A capacity or rate refusal creates neither a new cooldown nor an admitted-rate slot. Only successful admission inserts an expiry tuple and increments the quota.

decision.because: Counterexample on 3c51594 (ROADMAP item 10): a failed read of the STATS map published zeros, a counter reset to Prometheus; the next good read then put the whole history into one window of the rate check and of defense::under_attack, which feeds the storm latch. a_failed_stats_read_keeps_the_last_counters_and_is_counted saw (0, 0, 0) after a failed read.

body.statement: A failed read of the XDP STATS map is unknown, not zero: the XDP counters, and the rates and the storm attack signal computed from them, keep their last good values, and the failure is counted (sokol_xdp_stats_read_failures_total).

decision.because: Counterexample on c51cdc9: a detection read its time before awaiting the table lock; a tick that won the lock forgot a strike the decision's At: still counted, and the node recorded an At: 56 ms before the tick it had applied, so replay reported a false MISMATCH (exit 1). Operator ban/unban/flush and detector retraction were moved to the same order; only the detection path has a witness.

body.statement: A local detection that waits for the table lock records a decision time no earlier than any time the table was advanced to while it waited, and submits its decision record before releasing the lock, so replay at the recorded time sees the table the node had.

decision.because: Counterexample on c51cdc9: audit_witness::witnesses_for verified the peer chain, then reopened segments in a second pass that checks no joins; an active segment swapped between passes supplied a witness the verified chain never held (hit within 1-3 scans). Witnesses are now collected inside visit_chain; monitor --regret had the same pattern.

body.statement: Sequence-zero segment headers use the fixed zero genesis chain; non-zero retained prefixes may have an unknown pruned predecessor. File replay and audit-head comparisons consume records in the same pass that verifies their record chains and segment joins; a failed scan returns no replay or witness verdict. Replay binds its result to the consumed prefix; incomplete active tails and non-text payloads prevent CLI 0, non-text payloads fence dependent context, and changed sealed-segment lengths refuse verification. Retain at most 128 mismatch examples and 32 insufficient reason prefixes of at most 512 UTF-8 bytes while preserving complete decision totals and separate non-text-record counts. Refuse more than 4096 retained rotated segments, excluding the active file. This does not authenticate the writer or establish an atomic filesystem snapshot.

decision.because: Counterexample on c51cdc9: the scan cut each call at its first ')', so drop_verdict(packet_len.min(u64::MAX), drop_reason::VFR_ANOMALY) was invisible and an unlabelled drop passed; a non-literal reason was skipped silently.

body.statement: A drop reason has a metric label exactly when the XDP program passes it to drop_verdict; the source scan that checks this sees every drop_verdict call whatever its length argument and refuses a reason it cannot name as drop_reason::IDENT.

decision.because: Mutation check (CI, PR #7): the drop counts and the merge-at-full and exact-end boundaries of restore were unwitnessed (12 surviving mutants). They are now observable and pinned.

body.statement: After a restore every bounded table holds no more than its runtime bound (claims and retraction records MAX_KNOWN_CLAIMS, events MAX_EVENTS, support targets MAX_SUPPORT_TARGETS), whatever the file holds; operator lifts are kept first and what is dropped is counted.

decision.because: Round 7 candidate on 27d0ea0: the id was alerts.len()+1, so after 50 alerts every new alert was 51.

body.statement: Operator alert ids strictly increase while the alert list is capped at 50.
In current detector writer layouts, `Reason` is opaque data: it cannot override leading `IP`/`TTL`/`Why`/`Protected` or appended `Claim`/`At`/`Event`/`Ttl`. The complete reason bytes are retained.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 3, 2026-10-10): with an operator ban on the target, RETRACT answered 'OK lifted' (INTEGRATIONS.md: nothing else held the block) while it stayed blocked; 'too many known claims' was answered 'OK refused protected'.

body.statement: A detector retraction is answered OK lifted only when nothing blocks the target on this node any more; a block still held by an operator, static or peer claim is answered as still held. A capacity refusal of a signal is answered as a capacity refusal, never as a protected target.

Decisions to report cooldown, rate and capacity refusals are separated by at least one monotonic second; each report generates at most one line per category. Fixed-size reporting state retains the difference between cumulative and reported counters, including across empty/error polls. For each category, generated report totals plus pending deltas equal its cumulative counter before saturation. A report decision clears pending deltas; filtered or delayed writes do not change accounting.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt 2026-10-10, confirmed with strace): records written by a handle that died before syncing were reopened with unsynced=0, so the next sync skipped fsync and offered them as the durable head. Fix: records found on open count as unsynced until the first sync.

body.statement: Only a fsynced head is offered. A peer adds at most one witness record per WITNESS_MIN_INTERVAL to this log, and a head that is not 64 lowercase hex is not recorded; both refusals are counted.

decision.because: Round-9 control hunt (2026-10-15): a ban, a local decision, a peer claim and a BlockSync claim each checked the policy before the table lock; one waiting through a host refresh added a newly protected address after the recheck (an operator ban held it indefinitely). All three race tests failed on their assertion before the fix; BlockSync also alone.

body.statement: Every path that adds or adopts a block (operator ban, local decision, peer claim, BlockSync) reads the never-block policy under the block table's lock, where the host refresh replaces it and rechecks the table: a decision that waited through a refresh does not enforce an address the refresh protected.

decision.because: Assertion-red subprocess regressions: a successful write command accepted 65537 stdout bytes, and a failing command returned 65537 bytes of stderr as its diagnostic. Bound both pipes while draining concurrently and refuse over-limit RIB input rather than treating a prefix as observed absence. (Re-proposed by Claude 2026-10-12 with --after FLOWSPEC-P1: FLOWSPEC-R13 is a prose section, not a table row, so the original anchor could not be accepted.)

body.statement: GoBGP command stdout is limited to MAX_COMMAND_OUTPUT_BYTES, per-family RIB stdout to MAX_RIB_BYTES and every stderr pipe to MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES. Overflow refuses the call, kills and reaps the direct child; truncated or excessive RIB bytes never establish observed absence or write authority. These are input-byte budgets, not a total RSS or remote rollback guarantee.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 3, 2026-10-10): a 1500-byte line was run as two commands with two replies, against control.rs 'one command per line, one reply line each'.

body.statement: The control socket runs one command per line: a line that reaches the 1024-byte limit without a newline gets one error, runs no command and closes the connection.

A queued offset is usable only for the same observed content token and inode. Otherwise checkpoint position is zero in the current file. A loaded resume anchor survives failed source open/seek until successful installation.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 3, 2026-10-10): a gobgp -j reply naming one destination twice (a foreign local path, then []) parsed as a healthy empty RIB, and the round wrote over the foreign path (FLOWSPEC-R3, R4).

body.statement: A RIB read that repeats an object key at any level is unusable: it classifies no path and authorizes no write.

decision.because: promoted by the owner

body.statement: A replay refuses a Cargo registry whose crate archives or unpacked sources are not crates.io packages of the received Cargo.lock, so the recorded registry digest is a function of the inputs and no other project's sources reach the candidate code; the index cache, public metadata without sources, is not restricted.

Successful admissions of one source IP are separated by at least cooldown. A capacity or rate refusal creates neither a new cooldown nor an admitted-rate slot. Only successful admission inserts an expiry tuple and increments the quota.

decision.because: Mutation check (CI, PR #14): the delivery deadline could become 'now - budget' (one attempt, no retry) and no witness failed. The new witness pins that the hook retries within its budget.

body.statement: The FastNetMon hook sends its report through the ACK-mode outbox within a bounded wait and reports delivery only after the node's recognized answer; no answer within the bound is a non-zero exit that says the report is lost.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 2, 2026-10-10): a claim id is the hash of its bytes, so a detection byte-identical to a claim retracted in the same millisecond (same target, reason and end: a source TTL, or a permanent policy) got the retracted id. It was reported as a new, applied claim and its resend became a duplicate, yet it was never in force. Fix: issue_own moves such a claim a millisecond later until its id is free.

body.evidence_text: `a_detection_refused_at_capacity_leaves_no_event_and_no_strike` (mutations "remember the event first" and "count the strike first" each fail it), `a_detection_after_a_same_instant_retraction_is_enforced`, `a_permanent_redetection_after_a_same_instant_retraction_is_enforced`
body.statement: A detection checks its event id, adds or merges the claim, then records the event, under one table lock. A resend of an event acted on within EVENT_MEMORY is a duplicate. A refused detection (here: the known-claims cap) records no event and counts no strike: a resend after capacity frees is decided afresh, and the next block of that target gets the TTL of its first strike.

decision.because: Counterexample on 3c51594 (ROADMAP item 10): SIGNAL:trap|... on the IPC socket was counted in sokol_detections_total{source="trap"}, as a trap hit of this node; an_adapter_cannot_be_counted_under_a_source_of_this_node saw the trap row move by 1.

body.statement: An adapter on the IPC socket cannot be counted under this node's own sources: a decision whose adapter names itself trap or telemetry counts as other in sokol_detections_total. It is enforced and audited as before, under the name it gave.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt 2026-10-10): a head witnessed for 0 records of a log whose start is pruned was reported confirmed although nothing retained was compared. Fix: it is Pruned (unknown).

body.statement: A head witnessed for "after N records" is compared with this log's record N-1 after both chains verify. A different chain value is a contradiction even when the rewritten chain verifies on its own; fewer records than witnessed is missing; a pruned record is unknown, never confirmed.

decision.because: Round 8 on 9387b10: OK lifted was answered before the state was on disk and the outbox does not resend after it; after SIGKILL and restart the claim and its support came back (10 of 10 rounds), in XDP and in FlowSpec, until the claim's own end.

body.statement: A detector retraction that changes the block table is answered only after the change is on disk, or with a warning the outbox does not take as final, so a crash after an OK lifted answer does not bring the block back.

decision.because: Review of #33: the proposed statement promised reproduction after a fresh isolated run, which its witnesses do not exercise (they test the evaluation of execution records and the bwrap profile; isolation is checked by check-counterexample-isolation.py and the rehearsal, outside CI). Also two of its witnesses skip without SOKOL_WARRANT_BIN; both gate runs now provide the released binary, so acceptance no longer blocks later pull requests.

body.statement: The portable counterexample pilot binds exact source bytes by content address, and contract history and witness bodies to recipient-selected owner signers; it refuses unsupported profiles and tampered bytes. It reports REPRODUCED only when the worker's execution record shows the named defect assertion-red and every repaired and restored witness passing, each status re-derived from that witness's own exit and output, never taken from the record's claim. Imported signed observations remain recorded claims and confer no owner acceptance, settlement or deployment authority. These witnesses check the record and the fixed isolation profile, not the isolation itself; that is checked by the rehearsal.

decision.because: ROADMAP item 9: the storm arithmetic moved to common::storm so that Kani proves it for every input (storm::proofs, calibrated by proof-task.py with three faults); the unit tests stay.

body.statement: The attack signal leaves out exactly the drops storm mode itself adds (strict-parse drops while storm adds STRICT_PARSE, fragment drops while it adds DROP_IPV4_FRAGMENTS) and nothing else: a malformed-header flood is an attack in every mode, so a storm cannot keep itself going on legitimate traffic.

decision.because: Round-9 control hunt (2026-10-15): two concurrent RELOAD_PEERS could interleave so the table took the newer trust store and the registry the older one (a revoked peer authenticated while its claims were no longer enforced); the race test failed on its assertion before the fix.

body.statement: A RELOAD_PEERS puts its trust store into the block table and the mesh registry under one table lock, so concurrent reloads leave both on the same store.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 4, 2026-10-12): emit_drop_event_sampled never wrote payload (256 of 300 bytes); bpf_ringbuf_reserve does not zero, so after the ring wrapped the field carried other packets' bytes, against the ABI comment 'the kernel side sets them all'.

body.statement: Every byte of a DropEvent record the XDP program submits to the events ring is written between reserve and submit, so no record carries bytes of an earlier one.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 4, 2026-10-12): after tick dropped a used lease at the claim's end, a 50 s wall step back and a resend gave the claim a second lease (R26-07: the bound is total per claim); a lift was undone by an 11 min step back without a restart, while ADR-0003 disclaimed that only between restarts. Owner chose option A. Witnesses added after the mutation check (PR #15).

body.statement: A wall-clock step back smaller than FORGET_GRACE, with or without a restart, neither renews a peer claim's used lease nor undoes an operator lift: both records live FORGET_GRACE past the claim's end; a larger step back can revive either, and that bound is the same for both.

decision.because: Counterexamples on d7e65e4: live heartbeat did not expose failed LIST_BANS freshness; a node-applied command with a lost reply was reported as generic failure. Readback also needs route/attempt binding and partial-list visibility.

body.statement: Operator ban readback is independently UNKNOWN, FRESH or STALE with the last successful observation time, monotonic age, reported total and bounded diagnostic. Failed or malformed reads preserve the last valid list without marking it fresh; heartbeat cannot refresh it; an obsolete attempt or changed control route cannot publish. Command responses distinguish CONFIRMED acknowledgement, REJECTED node response, NOT_SENT before write and UNKNOWN after an attempted write without a valid complete reply. Confirmation is acknowledgement, not proof of kernel enforcement; LIST_BANS describes operator bans and may be partial.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 4, 2026-10-12): under_attack counted every drop reason, including drops storm mode itself causes, so legitimate fragmented or unparsable traffic could keep nodes under attack and the latch from ever seeing calm (ADR-0006: a cost bounded by the storm). Owner chose option A: a separate ABI reason for strict-parse drops. Witnesses added after the mutation check (PR #15).

body.statement: The attack signal leaves out exactly the drops storm mode itself adds (strict-parse drops while storm adds STRICT_PARSE, fragment drops while it adds DROP_IPV4_FRAGMENTS) and nothing else: a malformed-header flood is an attack in every mode, so a storm cannot keep itself going on legitimate traffic.
`AuditHead` goes only to peers whose handshake announced `audit-head`; a handshake without `features` parses (older nodes). Other commands go to every peer as before.

decision.because: Measurement R5 on 3c51594 (ROADMAP item 10): PeerRegistry::open_at held the shared replay mutex across the ML-DSA-65 verification, so all inbound verification ran one connection at a time on one core; a_signature_is_verified_without_holding_the_replay_lock times out on that code (no answer in 10 s while another thread holds the lock). Signature and clock window are now checked before the lock; only the replay lookup and insert run under it, still only after a valid signature.

body.statement: An inbound envelope's sender, ML-DSA signature and clock window are checked without the shared replay lock, so connections verify in parallel: a forged envelope is refused while another connection holds the lock. Only the replay lookup and insert run under it, and only after the signature verified, so unknown senders cannot fill the cache.

decision.because: Counterexamples (hunt round 3, 2026-10-10): a state file named *.tmp was its own temporary file and rewritten in place (the twin of SUR-C2 missed in round 1); an unreadable state file was not kept aside (ADR-0004) and was lost on the next write.

body.statement: The state file is replaced atomically through a temporary file named after it (its name plus .tmp), whatever its name; an unreadable or unparseable regular state file is kept aside under the first free .corrupt name before any later write.

decision.because: Requirement (ROADMAP, percolation row and item 10): a peer whose detector misfires, or a compromised peer within its envelope, spreads its blocks to every node that takes them; until now only the aggregate sokol_blocks_active showed it, once the map filled.

body.statement: Every claim a peer sends, by Claim or BlockSync, is counted under its issuer and what this node did with it (enforced, held, refused, known) in sokol_mesh_claims_total; the first MAX_ISSUERS issuers get their own label, later ones count as other. SokolPeerClaimSurge fires when one issuer's enforced and held claims surge.
Only a fsynced head is offered. A peer adds at most one witness record per WITNESS_MIN_INTERVAL to this log, and a head that is not 64 lowercase hex is not recorded; both refusals are counted.

decision.because: Counterexample on c51cdc9: every enforced block (Suricata, CrowdSec, telemetry) and every sampled XDP drop was sent as TIER=Tier1BotTarpit, so the operator's tier-1 trap card counted them and one trap hit counted twice. Producer-side twin of OPERATOR-T1.

body.statement: The node reports a trap tier only for a trap hit: an enforced local block is sent as TIER=LocalBlock and a sampled kernel drop as TIER=KernelDrop, tiers that move no trap tier counter (OPERATOR-T1).

Once quiescence returns, registered listeners and accepted IPC/control children have been dropped; they cannot mutate the final table snapshot or submit records after the terminal audit submission. Child registration is closed before cancellation, including concurrent registration.
Capacity refusal is reported as `refused` in audit/metrics and `OK refused retraction state capacity` over IPC. The outbox classifies it as a final refusal, not a recorded lift or transport retry.

Переповнення та ввімкнений дедлайн можуть прибрати його як окремо обліковану локальну втрату; запис у сокет сам по собі не є підтвердженням.

Witness helpers and runtime implementation are not pinned by witness-body hashes.
annotations.question: Коли адаптер може прибрати повідомлення з черги?

New delivery guarantees require a separate accepted decision.

body.statement: Transport failure, unknown reply or missing terminating LF retains an unexpired obligation. A complete recognized final reply removes it; bounded overflow and an opt-in forwarding deadline are explicit, separately counted local loss paths. ACK outcome is node acceptance/refusal, not proof of durable storage or completed kernel enforcement.

decision.because: Review of #26 (a purge then a clock step back accepted the original again) and the owner's choice of the fail-closed variants; amended after the review of #27: the honest-admission proof covered the purge floor, not the startup fence (a peer 2 ms behind was refused right after the start with no clock step), and the fence does not refuse an envelope the previous process accepted with a later stamp. common::replay proves the purge policy for any clock history, that a purge refuses no honest fresh envelope while this node's clock does not step back, the fence, and that the fence refuses no fresh envelope from MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_MS after the start on; proof-task.py calibrates each with a fault.

body.statement: An envelope accepted in this process is refused again at any moment it is fresh, whatever this node's clock did: while its nonce is remembered, and after that because its timestamp lies at or below its sender's floor, which a purged nonce raises (before_window). A new process refuses envelopes stamped before its start; one the previous process accepted with a later stamp is accepted again. While this node's clock does not step back, a purge puts no honest fresh envelope under a floor, and the startup fence can refuse honest envelopes (a sender whose clock is behind, envelopes in flight across the restart) only during the first MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_MS after the start (Kani: common::replay).

body.evidence_text: `invalid_input_cannot_evict_a_queued_signal`, `a_full_queue_drops_the_oldest_and_counts_it`; actual process restart/ACK cases below exercise cursor alignment.
body.statement: At checkpoint time, queued positions correspond to the remaining FIFO outbox entries. Only successful push adds a position; overflow removes the oldest pair; forwarding expiry drops its request/deadline pair; after flush the loop trims positions to remaining pending length. Outbox request/deadline entries are likewise paired.

decision.because: Round 7 candidate on 27d0ea0: a client trickling a byte per read (each read waits up to 8 s), or one that never reads a tarpit's writes, held one of the 256 trap slots indefinitely, and the ban came only when the session ended.

body.statement: A trap session holds its connection slot at most MAX_SESSION (300 s), however the client paces its reads or writes; a session the deadline ends still blocks its source, with that reason.

decision.because: Counterexample on 3c51594 (ROADMAP item 10, round-5 mesh candidate): mesh_dispatch read the time before waiting for the block table, so a claim adopted after a 1.5 s wait got a lease cap 1.5 s short; a_wait_for_the_table_does_not_shorten_a_peer_claims_lease saw the claim lifted before 600 s from when the table took it.

body.statement: A peer claim's local lease starts when the block table takes it (Claim and each claim of a BlockSync): a wait for a busy table does not shorten the lease, and the local cap still ends it.

decision.because: Round 8 on 9387b10: a flush or unban of more than about 1,900 own claims was one Retract frame over MAX_FRAME_BYTES; peers bailed before reading it and lost the retraction until the next connection's snapshot.

body.statement: Every retraction of this node's own claims that it broadcasts is packed into frames within SNAPSHOT_PAYLOAD_BUDGET, full and in order, so no retraction frame exceeds the transport limit and makes peers drop the connection with it.

A recorded retraction capacity refusal that the fresh replay cannot reproduce is unverified. Its speculative table is discarded; dependent decisions are insufficient until a new usable start record. It is neither a verified refusal nor a cascade of mismatches.

decision.because: Mutation check (CI, PR #8): forget_known could be replaced by () or its == 0 by != and no witness failed, so the per-issuer count could drift silently. The new witness pins that a share frees exactly as the claims of a peer end.

body.statement: A peer's claims known here, enforced or waiting, never exceed its envelope's known-claims share, and peers' claims together leave the room kept for this node's own decisions: no volume from one peer makes this node refuse its own detections or another peer's claims.

decision.because: Counterexample on c51cdc9: a peer claim ending at 590 s under a 600 s cap had no lease record; after a 500 s step back and a resend it was enforced again until 605 s past its start. Every enforced peer claim now records its lease end.

body.statement: A wall-clock step back smaller than FORGET_GRACE, with or without a restart, neither renews a peer claim's used lease, including a claim whose own end lies within the cap, nor undoes an operator lift: both records live FORGET_GRACE past the claim's end; a larger step back can revive either, and that bound is the same for both.
Explicit loss markers fence dependent replay until a usable start. Any marker prevents CLI 0, including a tail/pre-context gap; known mismatches retain 1.

decision.because: Counterexamples on c51cdc9: a never-authenticated connection had 50 replayed handshakes signature-checked (replay was skipped, not refused, before authentication); one pinned peer authenticated 4 connections (up to the listener's 100), outside ADR-0013's two-per-pair bound. The two other witnesses kill the mutants that widened the refusal.

body.statement: A connection whose first frame does not authenticate is closed, a replayed copy of a valid frame included, so an unauthenticated connection costs at most one signature verification; after the handshake a replayed frame is ignored. A pinned peer holds at most two authenticated connections, the bound from which inbound_worst_case and REPLAY_PER_SENDER are derived; a third is refused, and other peers' connections do not count against it.

body.evidence_text: `a_read_error_preserves_completed_alerts_and_unfinished_bytes`, `read_errors_before_a_complete_line_preserve_the_cursor_and_retry_bytes` (fault injected through the actual buffered scanner).
body.statement: Complete records read before a later I/O error are returned alongside the error; unfinished bytes and their starting position survive for retry. Byte/line quotas still apply.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 4, 2026-10-12): --storm-threshold=-0.1 made 0 of 3 attacked nodes a DistributedStorm and the latch kept strict mode on for good (ADR-0006); 50 or NaN silently disabled storm defense.

body.statement: The storm threshold is a share of live nodes, finite and in [0, 1); any other value is refused at startup, so a cluster with no attacked node is never a distributed storm.

When an identified event requires lifting/shortening own detector claims, capacity is checked for every missing retraction record, owner entry and replacement claim before support removal or replay-marker insertion. Capacity refusal preserves claims, support and event memory; after capacity is freed the same explicit request remains eligible.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt 2026-10-10): a cursor file named *.tmp was its own temporary file (with_extension), truncated in place before the new bytes were synced; a write failure left neither the old nor the new cursor. Fix: the temporary file is the cursor's name plus .tmp.

body.evidence_text: `a_damaged_cursor_rereads_the_log_instead_of_skipping_it` (empty, truncated and non-JSON cursors; mutation "damaged = missing" fails it), `a_cursor_is_replaced_not_rewritten_in_place_whatever_its_name`
body.statement: The saved cursor is replaced durably (temporary file synced, renamed, directory synced). A cursor file that exists but cannot be read or parsed starts reading the current file from its start, never its end; a missing cursor follows `--from-start`. Re-read alerts are bounded by the forwarding age and deduplicated by event id at the node.

decision.because: Round 7 on 27d0ea0: a peer's claim reason with a newline was written unescaped into the line-framed telemetry stream as extra HEARTBEAT/DB_LOG/DROP_IMMEDIATE lines, which the operator attributed to the node (control route redirected, readback reset, counters moved); the trap wrote attacker bytes as SNIPPET= outside VEC, so typed |TIER= chose the operator's tier.

body.statement: Text a mesh peer or a trap client controls reaches the operator's telemetry only inside the terminal VEC field and without line breaks: a mesh block's reason is stripped of control characters, and the trap's captured bytes follow VEC=. Neither can add telemetry lines (a heartbeat, a control route, a ban) nor choose a tier or an IP.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 3, 2026-10-10): a state file with MAX_KNOWN_CLAIMS + 1 retraction records restored all of them, past the bound the runtime enforces (block_table MAX_KNOWN_CLAIMS doc).

body.statement: After a restore every bounded table holds no more than its runtime bound (claims and retraction records MAX_KNOWN_CLAIMS, events MAX_EVENTS, support targets MAX_SUPPORT_TARGETS), whatever the file holds; operator lifts are kept first and what is dropped is counted.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt 2026-10-10): parse accepted node=+1, records=0003 and upper-case hex, which statement never writes, and a file named for another statement than it holds was confirmed or skipped. Fix: only the canonical line parses; a file not named after its statement is malformed.

body.statement: (ADR-0022, opt-in) A head statement is one exact line, written durably once and never rewritten; the node contacts nothing. `--verify-anchors` checks the log against every statement for this node; a file named like a statement that is not one fails the check.

decision.because: Counterexample on c51cdc9: renaming xdp_mode generic, class urgent or detection result pending left check-monitoring.sh green while SokolXdpGeneric, SokolUrgentBroadcastsDropped and SokolDetectorSurge could no longer fire.

body.statement: Every metric name and every label value that an alert rule or the dashboard selects on is rendered by the node; scripts/check-monitoring.sh refuses a rename of either.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 4, 2026-10-12): sokol-fastnetmon-notify connected, wrote and logged 'sent' with no ACK handshake and no answer read, against AGENTS.md (detector input goes through delivery::Outbox in ACK mode).

body.statement: The FastNetMon hook sends its report through the ACK-mode outbox within a bounded wait and reports delivery only after the node's recognized answer; no answer within the bound is a non-zero exit that says the report is lost.

decision.because: Counterexample on b75821f: a Tier2 record with TIER=Tier1BotTarpit inside VEC increments Tier1; key-shaped vector text can supply IP, and missing/invalid node IDs become node 0/1. Restoring that production handler with the four new regressions gives four assertion failures (11 preserved tests pass).

body.statement: Operator HEARTBEAT and DB_LOG require an explicit valid u32 node identity; malformed identities are ignored rather than attributed to node 0 or 1. In DB_LOG, tier counters use only exact known TIER fields and IP comes only from the header before terminal VEC; the entire VEC remainder is opaque diagnostic text. An unknown tier remains alert-visible without incrementing a known-tier counter. These are reported telemetry fields, not proof of a trap or kernel action.

decision.because: Mutation check (CI, PR #7): end < longest could become <= and no witness failed; a remaining reason with the same end keeps the block still held, not shortened to the same end.

body.statement: Retracting a detector reason that held a target longer than its other reasons shortens the block to the latest remaining end: the target stays blocked until then and is released after. A reported shortening is never a lift.

body.evidence_text: `a_partially_reproduced_audit_is_not_a_successful_cli_result` (real chained files and `print_report`), XDP smoke requires zero insufficient decisions
body.statement: Any insufficient decision prevents CLI success even when earlier/later decisions reproduce. Actual mismatches retain exit 1; complete nonempty replay has exit 0; incomplete/empty replay has exit 2.

(ADR-0022, opt-in) A head statement is one exact line, written durably once and never rewritten; the node contacts nothing. `--verify-anchors` checks the log against every statement for this node; a file named like a statement that is not one fails the check.

decision.because: Round 7 on 27d0ea0: command_json discarded the reply of a CONFIRMED outcome, so ADR-0005's 'OK ...; WARNING: not yet durable' reached the operator as a plain confirmation.

body.statement: A node's confirmation that carries a warning (OK ...; WARNING: not yet durable) keeps that warning, bounded to 512 characters, in the operator API's answer and on the dashboard; the outcome stays CONFIRMED.

decision.because: Round 7 on 27d0ea0: a pack's scripts/json.py was imported by the recipient's owner gate and ran unsandboxed during inspect/view/export/replay; a later phase on another source was hidden behind an earlier failure; view accepted a refused observation claiming a native pass; names colliding on case-insensitive filesystems and records citing absent blobs were accepted.

body.statement: Received pack data never runs in the recipient's tools: the recipient's owner gate runs isolated, so the pack's files cannot shadow its imports. inspect reads every blob a record cites against its address; descriptor names that collide after case folding or Unicode normalisation are refused; every phase's source snapshot is compared before any phase is classified; a refused or source-mismatched observation carries no native verdict and any other exactly one, matching its report.

The parsed command pacing rate is a `NonZeroU32`. Zero is rejected by `Args::parse` before outbox construction, LAPI polling or IPC; a zero rate cannot silently become one command per second. Default 200 and positive `u32` bounds remain valid, and zero poll interval remains a separate valid policy.

body.evidence_text: `client_logs_cannot_supply_replay_authority` (real writer/reader/CLI), XDP smoke client ACK/dump/fresh-replay checks
body.statement: Signal-socket `DB_LOG` text has a fixed `CLIENT_LOG` outer tag and cannot supply node lifecycle/decision/loss records.

decision.because: Round-9 closure of the MESH-N1 limit (ADR-0029): an envelope the previous process accepted with a stamp after the new start was accepted again; the floors saved with the state refuse it. Live: bench/mesh.sh floors F1-F3, control without the wiring fails F1/F3.

body.statement: A restarted node starts each trusted sender's replay window at or above the floor the previous process saved with its state, so an envelope that process accepted is refused again, even stamped after the new start, if a state write after its acceptance reached disk; a sender silent since keeps its floor, a floor is never lowered, and a sender no longer trusted gets none. The saved floors are bounded by MAX_MESH_FLOORS within MAX_STATE_BYTES.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 3, 2026-10-10): signal, the target becomes a host address (claim suspended, ADR-0012), RETRACT answered 'OK nothing held' and broadcast nothing; when the address left the host the block came back on a reason the detector took back, and peers kept enforcing it.

body.statement: A retraction that removes an event's support retracts, mesh-wide, every own detector claim on the target that no remaining support holds, also one the protected set suspends now; such a claim does not come back when the target leaves the host.

For positive rate `r`, requested pause `n` is the smallest whole-nanosecond interval satisfying `n * r >= 1,000,000,000`. Thus `1 <= n <= 1,000,000,000`; `(n - 1) * r` is insufficient. Integer ceiling avoids a shorter fractional rounding or zero pause at large rates.

decision.because: Requirement (AGENTS.md: a parser of bytes the node does not control gets a Kani proof): SecureEnvelope::decode reads every frame of any connection before authentication but lived in orchestrator, outside the proofs. Its framing moved to common::wire; wire::proofs prove it, calibrated by proof-task.py with three faults.

body.statement: A frame is a v2 envelope only if it starts with SKM and a version this node speaks; decoding any frame returns, and an accepted frame's header, payload and signature account for every byte, the payload exactly as long as its header says; what the node writes splits back into the same header, payload and signature (Kani: common::wire, frames up to HEADER_LEN + 6 bytes).

decision.because: ADR-0029 / MESH-N2: with floors saved in the state file, an envelope the previous process accepted with a later stamp is refused; without them (an older file, a lost write) MESH-N1's limit stands as stated.

body.statement: An envelope accepted in this process is refused again at any moment it is fresh, whatever this node's clock did: while its nonce is remembered, and after that because its timestamp lies at or below its sender's floor, which a purged nonce raises (before_window). A new process refuses envelopes stamped before its start; one the previous process accepted with a later stamp is accepted again unless its sender's floor was saved with the state after it (MESH-N2). While this node's clock does not step back, a purge puts no honest fresh envelope under a floor, and the startup fence can refuse honest envelopes (a sender whose clock is behind, envelopes in flight across the restart) only during the first MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_MS after the start (Kani: common::replay).

Cooldown membership and expiry FIFO describe the same distinct addresses; each has at most `COOLDOWN_CAP` = 100,000 entries. Start empty; remove the expired prefix from both; refuse at capacity before inserting into both. Never evict an unexpired address to admit another.

decision.because: Round 7 on 27d0ea0: a ban kept in the table after a failed kernel write was answered ERR, so the serving loop skipped the disk wait (R26-04) and the operator showed REJECTED while LIST_BANS listed the ban.

body.statement: An operator BAN that the block table keeps while its kernel write is retried is answered OK (kernel update pending), like UNBAN's pending removal, so it waits for its generation on disk and is not shown as a refusal.

annotations.agent_objective: Reproduce a counterexample without weakening the preserved statement or witnesses.
annotations.answer: Повна розпізнана кінцева відповідь вузла завершує зобов’язання. Невідома чи незавершена відповідь залишає непрострочене повідомлення в черзі. Переповнення та ввімкнений дедлайн можуть прибрати його як окремо обліковану локальну втрату; запис у сокет сам по собі не є підтвердженням.
annotations.coverage_gap: The legacy evidence text says overflow test above; IPC-A1 pins only the two named ACK witnesses. Overflow/deadline coverage requires separately inspecting SUR-Q1 and IPC-T1.
non_claims: ACK does not prove durable storage or completed kernel enforcement.
No exactly-once delivery, durable outbox or eventual progress guarantee.
Witness helpers and runtime implementation are not pinned by witness-body hashes.
annotations.question: Коли адаптер може прибрати повідомлення з черги?
annotations.scope: ACK-mode delivery::Outbox; unexpired queued obligations; adapter-to-node acknowledgement.
stop_conditions: Changing the pinned statement or witnesses requires owner re-pin.
New delivery guarantees require a separate accepted decision.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt 2026-10-10): a recognized line already buffered before a signal was written was taken as its answer. A node answering one request with two lines settled the next signal, whose own answer was unknown, as Applied; a line appended to the ACK answer retired a signal the node never answered. Fix: Conn::exchange refuses bytes that arrived before the request and drops the connection, keeping the signal queued.

body.statement: Transport failure, unknown reply or missing terminating LF retains an unexpired obligation. A complete recognized final reply removes it; bounded overflow and an opt-in forwarding deadline are explicit, separately counted local loss paths. ACK outcome is node acceptance/refusal, not proof of durable storage or completed kernel enforcement.

decision.because: Assertion-red bounded-report and torn-tail vectors on a06be0c; the old CLI returned 0 after a second-open replacement by an individually valid segment with a broken join. A sealed-segment growth vector exposed an incomplete streaming implementation before its correction. A real sequence-zero/nonzero-seed byte vector was accepted despite the fixed genesis specified by the record format.

body.statement: Sequence-zero segment headers use the fixed zero genesis chain; non-zero retained prefixes may have an unknown pruned predecessor. File replay and audit-head comparisons consume records in the same pass that verifies their record chains and segment joins; a failed scan returns no replay or witness verdict. Replay binds its result to the consumed prefix; incomplete active tails and non-text payloads prevent CLI 0, non-text payloads fence dependent context, and changed sealed-segment lengths refuse verification. Retain at most 128 mismatch examples and 32 insufficient reason prefixes of at most 512 UTF-8 bytes while preserving complete decision totals and separate non-text-record counts. Refuse more than 4096 retained rotated segments, excluding the active file. This does not authenticate the writer or establish an atomic filesystem snapshot.

decision.because: ROADMAP typed-axiom step: signal target selection used diagnostic strings as protection identity. Typed constructors and exhaustive SourceRole separate identity from wording while preserving current policy and messages. A native mutation restoring string-based target selection fails the matching-diagnostic assertion; compile controls require E0004 in source_role for a new variant, with explicit-role positive controls.

body.statement: Protection identity and diagnostic text are separate. For a protected single-address signal source, LocalAddress and HomeNetwork select the destination; every other declared protection role refuses redirection. Production ProtectionReason has no diagnostic-string conversion; legacy fixture conversions exist only under cfg(test). In the production protection module, adding a reason variant without an explicit source_role decision fails exhaustiveness checking; this requires a decision, not proof that the new decision is correct.

decision.because: Counterexample R5-F1 on c51cdc9: node 3 replayed the handshake node 2 had sent it to node 1, which authenticated node 3's connection as node 2 and sent node 1's broadcasts for node 2 to node 3. A recipient/nonce in the handshake would not stop a live two-way relay; the WireGuard tunnel address is authenticated by the peer's tunnel key (ADR-0027, owner chose B on 2026-10-12).

body.statement: A pinned node that the peers file binds to an address authenticates only on a connection from that address: a handshake from any other source is refused and counted (sokol_mesh_handshakes_wrong_address_total), so another peer cannot relay its handshake and take over delivery to it; a reload that binds it elsewhere closes its connection on its next envelope. One address cannot be bound to two nodes. A node bound to no address is accepted from any address and named at startup.

decision.because: Counterexample on 3c51594 (ROADMAP item 10, round-5 mesh candidate): after RELOAD_PEERS revoked node 2 and bound node 3 elsewhere, both still received every broadcast until their own next envelope failed (up to ~10 s); a_reload_stops_broadcasts_to_a_revoked_or_moved_node_at_once saw [2, 3, 4] reached instead of [4].

body.statement: A reload that stops pinning a connected node, or binds it to an address it is not connected from, unregisters its connections at once: no broadcast of this node reaches it after the reload, and the audit record PEERS_RELOADED names those nodes (Unregistered). Their connections still close on their next envelope (MESH-A2).

body.evidence_text: `a_timed_out_cleanup_worker_is_cancelled_and_joined`, `local_decision_is_audited_before_cancellable_mesh_publication` (actual registry lock held); XDP final-state/audit checks
body.statement: A cleanup-worker timeout cancels and joins the task instead of detaching it. Table mutation and its decision audit submission precede cancellable network awaits.

body.evidence_text: `a_damaged_cursor_rereads_the_log_instead_of_skipping_it` (empty, truncated and non-JSON cursors; mutation "damaged = missing" fails it).
body.statement: The saved cursor is replaced durably (temporary file synced, renamed, directory synced). A cursor file that exists but cannot be read or parsed starts reading the current file from its start, never its end; a missing cursor follows `--from-start`. Re-read alerts are bounded by the forwarding age and deduplicated by event id at the node.

decision.because: ROADMAP item 9: the lease arithmetic moved to common::lease so that Kani proves it for every input (lease::proofs: a resent claim never outlasts its first lease, a record only moves earlier, within FORGET_GRACE a live resend finds its record; calibrated by proof-task.py with three faults). Lease and lift records now share common::lease::kept, so the bound is the same for both by construction. The unit tests stay.

body.statement: A wall-clock step back smaller than FORGET_GRACE, with or without a restart, neither renews a peer claim's used lease, including a claim whose own end lies within the cap, nor undoes an operator lift: both records live FORGET_GRACE past the claim's end; a larger step back can revive either, and that bound is the same for both.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 2, 2026-10-10): with reasons B (60 s) and A (600 s) at one instant, retracting A answered 'shortened' but unblocked the target at once: the reissued shorter claim collided with B's retracted claim id and was born retracted. No contract stated the shortening boundary (ADR-0019), so it becomes one.

body.statement: Retracting a detector reason that held a target longer than its other reasons shortens the block to the latest remaining end: the target stays blocked until then and is released after. A reported shortening is never a lift.

body.evidence_text: Code structure plus mixed renewal/refusal history in `gate_generated_history_preserves_cooldown_and_bounded_unique_memory`; this is accounting, not a timing benchmark.
body.statement: Expiry inspection is an ordered prefix, with no full-set scan on each hot-cache refusal. Each admitted tuple is appended once and popped at most once. Thus total expiry pops cannot exceed prior successful admissions; each attempt adds at most one stopping head inspection.

CLI parsing rejects an age interval that cannot be added to the startup local `Instant`, before source/cursor/IPC operations. Zero and normal intervals remain valid configuration; each later per-alert addition is independently checked. This does not promise representability forever for values close to the clock limit.

decision.because: Counterexample an_explicit_large_peer_share_can_exhaust_the_shared_peer_budget: a configured 196608-record peer share fills the aggregate peer budget and a different peer is refused while an own detection is admitted. Clarify configuration-dependent availability; preserve all existing witnesses and add atomic reload/revocation coverage. Supersedes the narrower reload-only intent MESH-K1-87538f12083b.

body.statement: A newly held peer claim is admitted only below both its issuer's known-claims share and the aggregate peer budget MAX_KNOWN_CLAIMS - OWN_RESERVE. Peer admission cannot consume the room reserved for own claims; own admission remains subject to total capacity. Per-peer shares do not reserve independent room for every peer: at the aggregate bound another peer is refused too. Trust/quota reload is atomic, refuses a trusted issuer's share below its held count, and permits trust revocation while retaining the revoked issuer's records and accounting envelope.

decision.because: Assertion-red restore regression accepted a saved claim reason longer than the writer can emit. Replace whole-file allocation with a buffered streaming decoder, enforce token/record/collection budgets, retain rejected bytes and preserve failed restore status.

body.statement: State restore checks the writer-derived MAX_STATE_BYTES budget and JSON string/atom wire budgets while streaming, before unrestricted serde string allocation. Every retained input collection and string fits its named writer/runtime limit; nested support reasons are bounded too. Over-limit input is Failed, never Fresh, and original bytes are kept aside where possible. One extra bounded record may be decoded at a collection boundary. These bounds do not establish an RSS limit or a filesystem latency guarantee.

decision.because: Review of #33, fixed in #36: a developer's whole registry made the digest change with every other project built, often exceeded the input budget and exposed other projects' sources.

body.statement: A replay refuses a Cargo registry whose crate archives or unpacked sources are not crates.io packages of the received Cargo.lock, so the recorded registry digest is a function of the inputs and no other project's sources reach the candidate code; the index cache, public metadata without sources, is not restricted.

A parsed timestamp consumes the configured age budget. Future timestamps grant at most that budget from observation. Integer conversion and local-clock addition are checked; stale/unrepresentable timestamps do not enqueue. Missing/invalid timestamps retain the untimed policy.

body.evidence_text: `a_flush_records_real_queue_overflow_without_a_following_record`, `idle_sync_records_real_queue_overflow_without_a_following_record`, `disconnected_final_sync_records_real_queue_overflow`, `a_failed_loss_notice_retains_its_count_until_recovery` (actual Full channels, writer loop and unavailable-path recovery)
body.statement: Queue loss is emitted before following data and every sync path: explicit Flush, idle timeout, disconnected final sync. A failed notice retains its sampled count; that record cannot bypass the notice. Cross-producer drop publication and send are not atomic.

A head witnessed for "after N records" is compared with this log's record N-1 after both chains verify. A different chain value is a contradiction even when the rewritten chain verifies on its own; fewer records than witnessed is missing; a pruned record is unknown, never confirmed.

decision.because: Round 7 twin of OPERATOR-T1 on 27d0ea0: monitor.rs took the last TIER= and IP= anywhere in a record and scanned the vector for an IP, so a trap client's typed |TIER=…|IP=… chose what the TUI showed (the INVARIANTS prose that allowed a later TIER= is reworded).

body.statement: The monitor's view takes a record's tier, IP, length and snippet from its header before a terminal VEC= only, first match wins: text a trap client controls supplies neither the shown tier nor the shown IP.

decision.because: Mutation check (CI, PR #7): still_blocks could use && instead of || and no witness failed; a wanted block the kernel map could not take must still count as blocking for the reply.

body.statement: A detector retraction is answered OK lifted only when nothing blocks the target on this node any more; a block still held by an operator, static or peer claim is answered as still held. A capacity refusal of a signal is answered as a capacity refusal, never as a protected target.

decision.because: Counterexample (hunt round 3, 2026-10-10): the default was 64512:(node_id & 0xFFFF), so nodes 1 and 65537 shared 64512:1 and would withdraw each other's rules on a shared gobgpd (ADR-0008).

body.statement: The default ownership community is 64512:<node-id>; a node id that does not fit 16 bits is refused at startup unless a community is given explicitly, never truncated.

decision.because: Mutation check (CI, PR #7): until_ms > now in own_standing could become >= and no witness failed; a claim ends at its exact end, so a retraction at that instant finds nothing standing.

body.statement: A retraction that removes an event's support retracts, mesh-wide, every own detector claim on the target that no remaining support holds, also one the protected set suspends now; such a claim does not come back when the target leaves the host.
